Competitor News.summary: Visa Las Vegas! Oracle Red Bull Racing
bullets: Oracle Red Bull Racing will run a golden chrome championship livery on Alisha Palmowski's No.21 Academy Programme car, with Visa's signature colours inspiring an electric blue gradient. It debuts at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit on Thursday 19 November, the final round of the 2026 F1 Academy season.

Palmowski, who won the F1 Academy title at the United States Grand Prix, will also wear a matching special-edition race suit. Visa said the collaboration celebrates her title and supports emerging athletes, and the team said it gives her a fitting send-off from F1 Academy.
Competitor News.copy:
Following her F1 ACADEMY title victory at the United States Grand Prix, Alisha will take to the track in Sin City with a bespoke golden championship livery, celebrating her title-winning season in style. The special-edition livery will make its debut at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit on Thursday 19 November, marking the final round of the 2026 season.

Commemorating her status as F1 ACADEMY Champion, every partner logo on the Red Bull Racing Academy Programme car and her No.21 will feature a golden chrome finish, set against an electric blue gradient backdrop inspired by Visa's signature colours. The design will be enhanced by a light-reactive metallic finish, creating a striking look fit for a champion under the bright lights of Las Vegas.

Competitor News.title: Santander and Working Title Launch Exclusive Collection for Formula 1 Fans
Competitor News.summary: Santander and Working Title Launch Exclusive Collection for Formula 1 Fans Roastbrief US
bullets: Santander, a global Formula 1 sponsor, has launched Fragmentos, a five-piece collection made with Brazilian brand Working Title, as part of its motorsport activity in Brazil. The pieces are an S Jacket, a polo shirt, a scarf, a cap and the Fragmentos Jacket, which incorporates sidepod sections from cars that previously competed in the series. The collection goes on sale from 3 November through Working Title's website.

Droga5 developed the strategy and creative concept for the collection. Singer Nicole Scherzinger, who has close ties to Formula 1, wore the S Jacket on arriving in Brazil. Santander will activate around the São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos. Santander Brasil's CMO Guilherme Bernardes said the aim is to bring Brazilian audiences closer to the worlds surrounding motorsport, reinforcing the bank's role as Formula 1's official sponsor in Brazil.
Competitor News.copy:
As a global sponsor of Formula 1, Santander is entering a new phase of its motorsport initiatives in Brazil with the launch of Fragmentos, a collection created in collaboration with Working Title, a Brazilian brand operating at the intersection of fashion, culture and community. With strategy and creative concept developed by Droga5, the exclusive pieces draw inspiration from the symbols, memories and visual codes that define the world of F1. The collection will be available beginning November 3 through Working Title’s website.

The idea was born from the emotional connection fans build with the sport. Cars, components and other elements that make their way onto the track become more than technical objects. They become physical records of races, drivers and defining moments. Fragmentos draws on this relationship, transforming symbols of the sport into pieces fans can now wear.

But the findings also show that brands do not necessarily need a league-wide agreement to benefit, with several team-level partnerships producing substantial returns.

Wider Sports News.title: NFL reportedly wants new rights deals in place by start of next season
Wider Sports News.summary: NFL reportedly wants new rights deals in place by start of next season Sports Media Watch
Wider Sports News.copy:
The timeline is accelerating for the NFL’s expedited media rights negotiations. John Ourand of Puck reported Thursday that the NFL is now believed to want its new media rights deals completed before the new season begins in September, earlier than the fall timeframe that had been previously reported. The league is expected to negotiate and announce its new deals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, Ourand wrote, with all of them taking effect immediately.

Technically, the NFL does not have the ability to exit its current media rights deals until after the 2029 season at the earliest (2030 for ESPN), but there is little expectation that any of the league’s partners will oppose the expedited talks. According to Ourand, it is believed that the new contracts will run through the 2033 or 2034 seasons, meaning that the existing rightsholders can lock up NFL rights for the next seven or eight years by agreeing to the early talks. Currently, the networks are guaranteed only four additional seasons if they choose to wait for the league’s contractual opt-out.

Wider Sports News.title: Analyst predicts Walmart as surprise buyer for sports media rights in 2027
Wider Sports News.summary: Analyst predicts Walmart as surprise buyer for sports media rights in 2027 Awful Announcing
Wider Sports News.copy:
The sports media rights marketplace is preparing for a shakeup. As the decade nears its end and the NFL almost certainly exits its current set of media rights deals, networks and streamers are preparing for what could be a monumental shift in the industry. Legacy broadcasters continue to consolidate or get spun off from their corporate parents, while streaming giants continue to battle each other for engagement. The NFL is the 3,000-pound gorilla in the room that will dictate how networks and streamers approach other media rights opportunities in the next several years.

Major properties that will be on the market before or during NFL negotiations include the 2030 FIFA World Cup (set to be awarded by the end of 2026), MLB, NHL, and Premier League (all of which expire in 2028), Big Ten and PGA Tour (2030), and NASCAR (2031).

The court granted the request of the Milan public prosecutor’s office, which alleges serious shortcomings in the bank’s anti-money-laundering controls. The bank stays open, though, and the order is not a conviction: that is why I believe Audi will leave the contract alone. The real risk lies in communications, because for a bank the product is trust.

Suppose you are the head of communications at a Formula 1 team. One morning the name written on your car is in the headlines for a reason that has nothing to do with overtaking. What do you do? bullets: A white paper from design firm Populous and advisory firm Comeback Ventures, released on Thursday, says training facilities are becoming a key sponsorship asset in professional women's sports. It cites Denver Summit FC, which converted future naming rights with CommonSpirit Health into upfront capital, and the Golden State Valkyries, whose partnership with Sephora U.S. includes naming rights to their 31,800-square-foot performance centre in Oakland.

Denver Summit used contracted CommonSpirit sponsorship payments as collateral for a loan to fund construction. The report argues legacy sponsorship models rely on metrics such as linear television viewership and static logo exposure. Wider Sports News.copy:
Professional women’s sports have entered a new era. For Denver Summit FC in the National Women’s Soccer League, it meant converting their future naming rights with CommonSpirit Health to upfront infrastructure capital. In the Bay Area, the WNBA Golden State Valkyries’ landmark partnership with Sephora went beyond a naming rights deal, fueling athlete-led storytelling and player-designed fashion events. Whether sponsoring a new league such as Unrivaled or investing in a unique opportunity such as the first performance center shared by WNBA and NWSL teams, women’s sports sponsors are leveling up.

Returning from Red Roses camp to prepare for a new Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR) season, Natasha ‘Mo’ Hunt was hit by the realisation of how much had changed. For the first time in three campaigns, Gloucester-Hartpury enter not as defending champions but as challengers; Saracens, the league’s first dynastic power, were restored to their throne in June with a final demolition job against the upstart Trailfinders. South Africa men’s 15s head coach Rassie Erasmus has been suspended for six international matches with immediate effect. The sanction follows a review of wide-ranging comments made by Erasmus at a media conference this week concerning officiating during the Springboks’ Nations Championship match against France last Friday.

An independent panel imposed the sanction under World Rugby’s Match Official Abuse Sanction Process. Introduced in July 2026 with national member unions, competitions, International Rugby Match Officials (IRMO) and International Rugby Players’ Association (IRPA) support, the process runs in parallel with Regulation 18 and provides a clear, consistent framework for addressing public criticism of match officials, particularly comments that may undermine the integrity of individuals or the sport, or fuel online abuse.

Rugby.title: 2027 Rugby World Cup: New format, draw and fixtures
Rugby.summary: 2027 Rugby World Cup: New format, draw and fixtures Ruck.co.uk
bullets: The 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia will expand from 20 to 24 nations, the first time that number has competed since 1999, with six pools of four. The top two in each pool and the four best third-placed teams will reach a new round of 16, so 16 nations advance. Teams play three pool matches instead of four, and champions will still play seven matches, with at least five rest days between games.

The tournament runs from 1 October to 13 November 2027 across seven Australian cities, opening with Australia against Hong Kong China in Perth. England and Wales meet in Pool F, Ireland are drawn with Scotland and Australia face New Zealand. Defending champions South Africa play Italy, Georgia and Romania, while England open against Tonga. The pool stage ends on 17 October, with the knockout stages beginning on 23 October.
Rugby.copy:
The 2027 Rugby World Cup will look very different, with the biggest overhaul of the tournament in more than two decades set to transform rugby's showpiece event. For the first time since 1999, the competition will feature 24 nations, with Australia preparing to host the biggest Rugby World Cup in history.

But the expansion is only half the story. World Rugby has introduced a completely new knockout stage, changed the pool structure and opened the door for teams finishing third to reach the last 16.

Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast is in danger of missing Saturday's Nations Championship match against South Africa after being cited for a tackle against Fiji. Prendergast will face a disciplinary process for a hip-drop tackle on Fijian captain Peceli Yato in the first half of Ireland's 43-15 win in Dublin on Saturday.

The technique, when a tackling player drops their hips and bodyweight on to the ball-carrier's legs, was outlawed by World Rugby before November's internationals and the 23-year-old is the first player to be cited over its use in a game.

Los Teros started the contest strongly. Center Juan Manuel Alonso scored in the 7th minute. The try had a centennial connection as Mateo Sanguinetti put in the assist pass in what was his 100th test match for Uruguay. His over the shoulder flick pass came after an excellent carry from Felipe Aliaga. Ícaro Amarillo added the conversion and Uruguay’s players had their heads up.

Rugby.title: Magnificent Wales beat New Zealand for first time since 1953
Rugby.summary: Wales celebrate a first victory against New Zealand since 1953 with a brilliant 35-28 win to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.
bullets: Wales beat New Zealand for the first time since 1953, ending a run of 34 straight defeats against the All Blacks, in a nine-try Nations Championship match at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. Tries from Tomos Williams, captain Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit put Wales 35-21 ahead. New Zealand replied through Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi, Fehi Fineanganofo and Peter Lakai, with Richie Mo'unga kicking four conversions.

Wales held the All Blacks up three times over the line in the final quarter, with flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins leading the defence. The attendance of 55,152 was the lowest for the 14 Wales–New Zealand matches at the stadium. New Zealand still moved above South Africa to top the southern section with one weekend of regular matches left, after France beat the Springboks on Friday.
Rugby.copy:
Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.

Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins.

Rugby.title: Mateo Sanguinetti Becomes Second Uruguayan Test Centurion and First Americas Prop to Reach 100 Caps
Rugby.summary: Mateo Sanguinetti Becomes Second Uruguayan Test Centurion and First Americas Prop to Reach 100 Caps Americas Rugby News
Rugby.copy:
When Mateo Sanguinetti runs onto the pitch at Trailfinders Sports Ground in London this Saturday to face Zimbabwe, the 34-year-old loose head prop will etch his name permanently into rugby history. Earning his 100th Test cap for Los Teros, Sanguinetti becomes just the second Uruguayan player, following former teammate Diego Magno, to reach the century mark, and the first prop from anywhere in the Americas to achieve the milestone.

Sanguinetti’s journey to 100 caps began in Montevideo at his beloved home club, Los Cuervos, where he started playing at age 10. After rising through Uruguay’s age-grade ranks, he made his senior Test debut against Paraguay in Asunción in April 2014. At the time, Uruguay was an amateur outfit battling to return to the global stage after missing consecutive tournaments. Sanguinetti immediately became part of the historic 2014 repechage qualifying campaign against Russia, culminating in the unforgettable victory in Montevideo that punched Uruguay’s ticket to Rugby World Cup 2015 in England and Wales.

Rugby.summary: Former Rugby World Cup captain handed 11-year ban from the sport Ruck.co.uk
bullets: World Rugby has banned former Georgia captain Merab Sharikadze for 11 years after he admitted supplying clean urine samples to three international teammates. The 104-cap centre, who led Georgia at the 2019 and 2023 Rugby World Cups, was one of seven people punished, with six players and a team doctor suspended. The governing body confirmed the bans in May 2026.

The investigation found players had swapped urine samples during drug tests. World Rugby found no evidence the scheme was designed to conceal performance-enhancing drugs, but said there was credible evidence it was meant to hide cannabis and tramadol use. The Georgia Rugby Union accepted a misconduct charge and a financial penalty. Sharikadze, who captained Georgia to victory over Wales in Cardiff in 2022, has since moved into mixed martial arts and won his debut in 2026.

Rugby.title: Maro Itoje warns England not to sleepwalk into clash with Eddie Jones’s Japan
Rugby.summary: Maro Itoje warns England not to sleepwalk into clash with Eddie Jones’s Japan The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Maro Itoje has insisted England will be ready for any curveballs Eddie Jones may throw on Saturday, warning his side they cannot “sleepwalk” into battle against Japan. Jones, England’s longest-serving head coach after his stint between 2015 and 2022, has strongly hinted he will set his side up to unsettle his former charges at Twickenham, warning that they do not like “unorthodox” rugby. The hosts are heavy favourites to back up last week’s record win over Australia with another emphatic victory and have never lost to Japan but Steve Borthwick has made 10 personnel and two positional changes, fielding an inexperienced side against that of his predecessor.

“The overarching message this week is that we need to be alive,” said Itoje. “It’s impossible to tick off every eventuality that an opposition might do, especially a team like Japan, who have a very distinct way of playing. They’re very consistent at getting speed into the game. They could do a number of things, so let’s be alive and let’s not sleepwalk into things and think ‘most teams play like this’ because Japan aren’t most teams.

Jasper Wiese was shown a 20-minute red card in the second half. France are six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere Nations Championship standings and face Argentina next Saturday, with the inaugural final at Allianz Stadium on Sunday, 29 November. South Africa play Ireland in Dublin.

Rugby.title: Beirne named captain as Ireland look to build on strong start
Rugby.summary: Tadhg Beirne, so often Ireland's 'Mr Dependable', leads the team's bid to improve on last week's win over Argentina against Fiji on Saturday.
bullets: Tadhg Beirne will captain Ireland at home for the first time against Fiji in Dublin on Saturday, deputising for the injured Caelan Doris and Dan Sheehan. He first captained Ireland in July's 36-20 Nations Championship win over Japan. Ireland make seven personnel changes and two positional switches from the 42-12 win over Argentina, with Ronan Kelleher, James Ryan and Josh van der Flier recalled to the pack and Jamison Gibson-Park, Bundee Aki, Jamie Osborne and Tommy O'Brien drafted into the backline.

Beirne said leading the side out at the Aviva Stadium was special, with his family attending, and that Ireland want to build on last week's performance before facing world champions South Africa next week. Ireland are third in the Nations Championship northern hemisphere table and have never lost to Fiji, winning 52-17 in Dublin in 2024. Fiji, now coached by Jake White, have lost all four matches, including a 54-17 defeat by France in Lyon.
Rugby.copy:

It comes just a month after the Welsh Rugby Union published evidence outlining how it decided why there should only be three teams in Wales from 2028, as well as where those sides are based. The controversial three-team policy was first suggested in October 2025, with the governing body finally publishing its evidence for issuing one licence in the east, one in the west and one in Cardiff a year later.

Rugby.title: Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams

bullets: Ospreys say a report they commissioned from Sheffield Hallam University concludes that Welsh rugby should not cut its professional clubs from four to three. The Welsh Rugby Union intends to drop a side by 2028, with the decision due by next summer, and Ospreys and Scarlets are competing for the west Wales licence. The report covers 23 seasons from 2003-04 and says the data does not support removing a team.

The report says derbies between the four clubs generated 48% of home league attendances in Wales from 2012 to 2026 and would fall from 12 a season to six with three clubs. It also warns of a player "bottleneck". It does not address in depth how four clubs could be afforded: the WRU has reported losses of £18m and wants to cut professional spending from £26m to £20m by 2028. The full report goes to the regions and the WRU later this month.

Rugby.title: Why England’s fringe figures face World Cup audition against Japan

Rugby.copy:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. When Eddie Jones was Steve Borthwick’s boss as England head coach, the vastly-experienced Australian explained to his assistant the concept of international rugby’s twin horizons. There is, always, the game immediately ahead, the importance of which must always be underlined to the squad. And then there is the second horizon of every cyclical sport: the World Cup, always occupying the plotting parts of a coaching staff’s minds.

It is that second horizon that has come more sharply into focus ahead of this game against Japan. Borthwick is always conscious of not getting too far ahead of himself, but, having made 10 changes and two more positional tweaks to his starting side from the win over Australia, spoke openly of the opportunity he had presented to some players. Of consideration, too, were the heavy workloads or recent injury returns for a Tommy Freeman or Fin Baxter – and that’s before even mentioning the injuries to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, George Furbank, Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson, even it is hoped that the latter trio will be fit for New Zealand next week.

Rugby.title: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement
Rugby.summary: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement Americas Rugby News
Rugby.copy:
Rugby Canada and USA Rugby have launched a four-year high-performance pathway agreement to unify player development and lock in a recurring annual calendar of cross-border competition. Rather than treating one another solely as fierce regional rivals, the two governing bodies are combining resources to build a shared ecosystem of senior test matches, joint training camps, and age-grade tournaments. This alliance establishes a predictable, long-term foundation designed to elevate North American rugby on the world stage over the next decade.

The four-year high-performance pathway agreement between USA Rugby and Rugby Canada builds upon one of North America’s longest-running sporting rivalries. Dating back to the first men’s test match in 1977 and the historic first women’s test outside of Europe in 1987, the two nations have frequently clashed across regional tournaments like the Churchill Cup, the Americas Rugby Championship, and the Pacific Nations Cup. While cross-border youth tours and joint developmental programming were a regular staple of North American rugby prior to 2020, those collaborative pathways were largely neglected in the post-COVID era. As a result, the rival unions often relied on sporadic, ad-hoc fixtures rather than a unified approach to player progression.

Racket.copy:

Alcaraz produced another sparkling display to control the contest throughout, despite ending the match with heavy strapping on his upper-left leg. The issue did not disrupt the world number three, who led by a set and a break when he received treatment on the area, as he cruised to a 6-2 6-4 win in just 72 minutes.

Racket.title: Rising star Fils earns first ATP Finals win
Racket.summary: Rising star Arthur Fils claims his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.
Racket.copy:
Rising star Arthur Fils claimed his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin. Fils, 22, beat 20-year-old Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 to become the first Frenchman to record an ATP Finals victory since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011.

It was the youngest match by combined age at the season-ending tournament - which features the eight top-performing men - since a 21-year-old Novak Djokovic defeated a 20-year-old Juan Martin del Potro in 2008.

Racket.title: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton to reach semi-finals
Racket.summary: ATP Finals: Alexander Zverev beats Ben Shelton to reach semi-finals BBC
bullets: World number one Alexander Zverev beat fourth-ranked Ben Shelton 6-2 7-6 (7-4) at the ATP Finals in Turin to reach the semi-finals with a match to spare. He lost two of 31 service points in the second set and extended his unbeaten run against Shelton to seven matches.

Zverev's win confirmed Rafael Jodar's elimination after Arthur Fils beat the Spaniard 4-6 6-2 6-2. Fils, the first Frenchman to win an ATP Finals match since 2011, plays Zverev on Thursday for a semi-final place. Britain's Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara lost their second doubles match.
Racket.copy:
World number one Alexander Zverev produced another serving masterclass against Ben Shelton to qualify for the ATP Finals knockout stage with a match to spare. The German, 29, lost just two of the 31 points played on his serve in the second set as he completed an impressive 6-2 7-6 (7-4) win over fourth-ranked Shelton.

The two-time champion only made 10 unforced errors and landed 25 winners in a ruthless display to reach the semi-finals at the season-ending tournament for a fifth time. Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticised the ATP's chairman and CEO for their absence at Monday's year-end world number one trophy presentation. Wimbledon champions Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara received their trophy from the ATP's chief tour officer Andre Silva in Turin, after ending the season as the top-ranked men's doubles pairing for the first time.

In his acceptance speech, Patten, 30, called out ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for their decision not to attend. "What a journey it has been. Turin is such a special place for us, we played a challenger just across the road when we ranked 60 and 40 in the world a couple of years ago. I never would have dreamt that we would be in the position that we're in now," said Patten.

Racket.summary: Alcaraz dispatches Tiafoe for opening win in Turin ATP Tour
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz opened his Nitto ATP Finals campaign with a 6-2, 6-2 win over Frances Tiafoe in 69 minutes at the Inalpi Arena in Turin on Monday 16 November. The second seed took a 4-0 lead early in the first set. In the second he saved three break points at 3-2, then served out the match after a backhand winner down the line.

The result puts Alcaraz at 1-0 in the Ivan Lendl Group, which also includes Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli, as well as Tiafoe. He leads Tiafoe 3-1 in their head-to-head and is making his fourth ATP Finals appearance, with a title-match loss to Jannik Sinner last year his best result. He has won consecutive titles in Paris and Vienna and is chasing his sixth title of the season and 30th at tour level. Tiafoe, 28, is making his debut at the event after winning 44 matches this year and a title in Halle.

Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Two years after falling one match short of the title at the WTA Finals, Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend got another chance to lift the trophy. This time, they made it count, defeating Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini 6-4, 6-3 on Sunday to capture their first FAGE WTA Finals title as a team and their sixth title of the season.

Siniakova and Townsend opened the week with a loss to the Italians in the group stage. Errani and Paolini, the last team to qualify for the season-ending tournament, had won all four of their matches en route to their first WTA Finals championship match. But the second seeds ended that unbeaten run on the same courts where they had won the Indian Wells title in March.

bullets: Lakshya Sen won the Kumamoto Masters Japan title on Sunday, beating home favourite Koki Watanabe 13-21 21-18 21-14 in 64 minutes. The World No. 13 claimed a second consecutive BWF Tour title, following the Hylo Open in Germany on 1 November. The Super 500 win earned him 9,200 ranking points.

Before the tournament, Lakshya, 25, was 12th in the Race to Finals standings on 64,980 points. He is expected to move to sixth, inside the top eight needed to qualify for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou. His place is not yet mathematically secured, with the Hong Kong Open from 17 to 22 November the final qualifying event. He said he kept his confidence up despite starting with a game down in many matches.

Racket.title: How it happened: Andreeva wins the FAGE WTA Finals on debut without dropping a set!
Racket.summary: How it happened: Andreeva wins the FAGE WTA Finals on debut without dropping a set! WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- We came to Indian Wells to see what Mirra Andreeva would do in her first FAGE WTA Finals. We’re leaving without ever seeing her play a third set. She won all five matches, took all 10 sets and finished the week with a 61-26 edge in games. And on Sunday, she beat the same player she’d opened against, this time with a trophy waiting for her at the end.

At 19, Andreeva’s 7-5, 6-3 win in 1 hour and 48 minutes against Elina Svitolina made her the youngest WTA Finals champion since Maria Sharapova in 2004. A straight-sets sweep on debut puts her in even rarer company. Chris Evert did it at the inaugural edition in 1972, and Serena Williams won three matches in straight sets in 2001 before taking the title by walkover.

bullets: Mirra Andreeva, 19, won the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Sunday, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 in the final. Koki Watanabe reached his second final of the year with a come-from-behind effort against Kunlavut Vitidsarn at the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026. Incidentally, Watanabe’s only other final this year was also on home soil – at the DAIHATSU Japan Open in July. The home hope trailed in the second half of the decider, with Vitidsarn taking a three-point lead at 18-15, but Watanabe was tenacious and saved one match point before converting his own second opportunity, 14-21 21-11 23-21.

In the final, Watanabe takes on Lakshya Sen, who made his second straight final. Sen, who won the HYLO Open a fortnight ago, got his first win over Alwi Farhan in three matches, 21-12 15-21 21-11.

Racket.title: Sabalenka's season ended by Svitolina at WTA Finals
Racket.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's season ends in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beats the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals.
bullets: Aryna Sabalenka's season ended at the WTA Finals as Elina Svitolina beat her 6-3 3-6 6-1 to reach the semi-finals. Sabalenka forced a deciding set but lost the last six games, two days after losing the final 11 games against Mirra Andreeva. Svitolina, 32 and the 2018 winner, will meet Czech world number eight Linda Noskova in the last four.

Sabalenka lost the finals at both the Australian Open and the US Open, so 2025 is her first season since 2022 without a major. She won three other titles, including the Indian Wells and Miami double, and had the tour's best win percentage at 81% (47-11). Elena Rybakina took the world number one ranking from her after 99 weeks. Andreeva, 19, beat Diana Shnaider 6-2 6-1 to complete a perfect group record and faces Jessica Pegula in the other semi-final.
Racket.copy:
Aryna Sabalenka's season ended in disappointment as Elina Svitolina beat the former world number one to claim her place in the knockout stage at the WTA Finals. Sabalenka took her frustration out on her racquet and reacted to losing a point by crouching to the ground at the back of the court as a semi-final place slipped away.

The Belarusian was able to force a deciding set after unravelling in the latter stages of the first, but lost the final six games in slumping to a 6-3 3-6 6-1 loss. It came two days after the four-time major winner lost each of the last 11 games as she was thrashed by Mirra Andreeva.

Racket.title: Kumamoto Masters: Sen Stays in Sight of Hangzhou
Racket.summary: Kumamoto Masters: Sen Stays in Sight of Hangzhou BWF World Tour
Racket.copy:
HYLO Open champion Lakshya Sen’s recent form continued to hold as he made the semifinals of the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026. The Indian did himself a big favour for his chances of qualifying to the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 in Hangzhou as he beat home hope Yushi Tanaka 21-16 21-15 to set up a last-four clash with No.6 seed Alwi Farhan, who has already qualified for the season finale.

Two others in contention for Hangzhou – Kunlavut Vitidsarn and Koki Watanabe – will face off in the other semifinal. In men’s doubles, Arctic Open champions Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King made their third semifinal from five tournaments, as they blew past Lee Jhe-Huei/Yang Po-Hsuan 21-16 21-12. The Malaysians take on Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard, who are among the frontline contenders to qualify for the season finale. In the top half, new combination Wang Chang/Xie Hao Nan face home duo Takuro Hoki/Yugo Kobayashi, who beat No.7 seeds Ben Lane/Sean Vendy in an hour-long quarterfinal.

bullets: Carlos Alcaraz cut short a practice session with Flavio Cobolli in Turin ahead of the ATP Finals after complaining of stomach discomfort. Racket.copy:

The tournament favourite arrived in Turin with taping on his right knee, after a hectic couple of weeks that have seen him lift indoor titles at the ATP 500 tournament in Vienna and then at last week’s Paris Masters.

While Alcaraz’s camp have played down any suggestion that the seven-time Grand Slam champion is struggling to be fit for the start of the ATP Finals, he has now been hit by another problem after complaining of stomach discomfort during his hitting session with Cobolli.

Coco Gauff made headlines when she brandished the WTA Finals as ‘kinda stupid’ after her defeat to Linda Noskova. “The scenarios, I know they make sense, but they’re kinda stupid. If I win my match [Thursday] and I still don’t qualify, I’m like, ‘It’s okay, it’s cool.’ I’m looking forward to next year. I can’t say much, but everybody knows that has to change,” said Gauff.

Gauff did win her final match at the WTA Finals, against Marta Kostyuk, but she didn’t qualify for the semifinals, missing out to Jessica Pegula. After confirmation that she would no longer play a part in the 2026 WTA Finals, she clarified what she meant when she called the format ‘stupid’.

Racket.summary: ATP partnership revenues rise 49% to record high ATP Tour
Racket.copy:
ATP has delivered its strongest partnership performance to date, with central partnership revenues rising 49% year on year in 2026. The increase sees ATP central partnership revenues surpass the $100 million mark for the first time. Since 2022, revenues have increased by more than 200%, driven by new agreements and expanded investment from longstanding partners such as Emirates, Infosys, Nitto, Lexus, Haier and Yokohama, some of which have worked with ATP for more than a decade.

This year’s growth was fuelled by new partnerships with EQT and K-Swiss, alongside continued investment from existing partners. Earlier this week, ATP also announced a multi-year partnership with Julius Baer, which becomes ATP’s first Official Wealth Management Partner and the first Official Partner of the ATP Coaches Programme, with activation across five ATP tournaments on three continents from 2027.

Racket.summary: British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker retires after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.
Racket.copy:
British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals. The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley.

A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season. At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles.

The professional golf world faces a new reality as the DP World Tour moves to fill its fields with high-profile names from the collapsing LIV Golf circuit. Nine players who left their original tours to join the Saudi-backed league have been offered a path back through sponsor invitations, a move that prioritizes star power over traditional meritocratic rankings. This shift comes as LIV Golf winds down through bankruptcy proceedings, leaving many players in limbo while tour officials scramble to stabilize the game's ecosystem.

According to Rediff, European Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings acknowledged the rapid shift in the sport, stating, "There has been significant change in the landscape of men's professional golf over the past 12 months." The tour is now offering these invitations without the hefty appearance fees that characterized the LIV era, aiming to inject excitement into lower-ranked events. This strategy targets specific stops that need a boost in star power, ensuring fields remain competitive even if depleted of top-tier members. According to Ronan MacNamara from Irish Golfer Magazine, up to 34 individuals previously associated with LIV are set to retain DP World Tour status in the coming year, a figure appearing inflated due to the former league's hostile maneuvers against the tour.

There are exciting times ahead on the DP World Tour after 19 former LIV golfers were given routes into the European circuit's ecosystem ahead of the 2027 campaign. The most high-profile name among them belongs to Bryson DeChambeau, who had previously indicated he was set on committing to the latest edition of LIV Golf before the team-based league was forced into liquidation.

However, with very few options left on the table due to the PGA Tour failing to offer any kind of fresh olive branch, DeChambeau submitted the necessary paperwork to become a DP World Tour member just hours before Sunday's deadline.

DeChambeau has joined as a 'Category 1' member as a recent Major winner, while many other big names have either earned status, rejoined or agreed sponsor invitation deals. Cameron Smith, Joaquin Niemann and Dustin Johnson are three of nine men to have agreed to a number of sponsor's invitations for certain events, while Ryder Cup legends Sergio Garcia, Lee Westwood and Ian Poulter have also rejoined.

For a time during Sunday's final round at the DP World Tour Championship, just one-tenth of a point separated Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy as the pair battled for the Race to Dubai crown.

Golf.title: After historic Sunday, Rory McIlroy bullish about more than just his own game
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy's Race to Dubai battle ended with a record-tying win and a glimpse of a bright future on the horizon. The post After historic Sunday, Rory McIlroy bullish about more than just his own game appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Sunday in Dubai ended with Rory McIlroy winning an emotional, history-tying eighth Race to Dubai title after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship, five shots behind winner Tyrrell Hatton. The second-place finish saw McIlroy narrowly pass Eugenio Chacarra, the 26-year-old Spaniard who finished tied for fourth, two shots behind McIlroy, for the season-long crown.

The victory left McIlroy emotional. After the win, McIlroy revealed that his father, Gerry, recently underwent a double lung transplant and that he spent nine days in the ICU. Rory said his father is doing well and told him to “go win the Race to Dubai,” which spurred McIlroy to chase down Chacarra and claim his record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title. The win further cemented McIlroy’s status as one of, if not the, greatest European golfers in history.

Golf.title: Don't fall for this common golf setup myth, says top teacher
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Doug Spencer explains why you shouldn't try to use the same setup position for every shot. The post Don’t fall for this common golf setup myth, says top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Ask ten golfers on the range what they’re thinking about at address and you’ll likely get ten different answers: Keep your head down. Bend 45 degrees at the hips. Square your feet. Keep your left arm rigid.

We’ve been conditioned to view the golf setup as a static checklist of rules — a rigid pose designed simply to hold us in place before the action begins. That mindset is one of the biggest reasons golfers struggle with consistency.

It is the first project of his new course design firm, DeChambeau Designs, in partnership with Clovis-based developer Cook Land Company. The site is the historic McFarlane Ranch. Plans include homes, a clubhouse, a public farmers market and programmes giving local youth and schools access to the sport.

The announcement comes as LIV Golf has shut down and players are seeking 2027 playing rights. DeChambeau's 2024 US Open win makes him eligible for full DP World Tour membership, but he has not confirmed whether he applied before the mid-November deadline. He is scheduled to play December's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa. Rory McIlroy said DeChambeau draws eyeballs to tournaments but does not appear to have many options.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf’s most successful player signs major DP World Tour deal Today's Golfer
bullets: Joaquin Niemann, who won nine individual events and earned $88m in prize money across five LIV Golf seasons, has signed a DP World Tour deal giving him between 15 and 20 tournament invites next season, according to Golf Channel Latin America. The invites are likely to fall between February and August and will not include the Rolex Series events.

The 28-year-old has no tour status but can play the circuit because it has offered packages of guaranteed invites to non-members returning from LIV. He remains banned on the PGA Tour until at least next August. Lucas Herbert is also set to sign a similar deal. The tour will confirm on 17 November whether Bryson DeChambeau, eligible through his 2024 US Open win, has taken a card for 2027.
Golf.copy:
A number of LIV Golf stars are converging on the DP World Tour, including the breakaway league’s most successful player. He earned $88million in prize money across his five seasons yet still did not top the inordinate earnings table at LIV Golf. But there can be no doubt that, with his nine individual victories, Joaquin Niemann was the most successful player on the now-doomed breakaway league.

What the Chilean’s dominance during this period will mean for his legacy can and will be disputed, but Niemann is returning to golf’s traditional tours as a winner on LIV, the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour.

Golf.title: First win for Duncan after 12 years & 222 attempts
Golf.summary: American Lindy Duncan wins The Annika for her first LPGA Tour title after playing in 222 events over 12 years.
bullets: American Lindy Duncan, 35, won her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd attempt at The Annika, finishing 16 under after a final-round 67 at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida. She began the day one shot ahead and was tied with South Korea's Choi Hye-jin with two holes left, before two late birdies secured a two-shot victory. Duncan joined the tour in 2014 and had only one top-10 finish this season.

The win lifted Duncan from 74th to 34th in the season-long points race, qualifying her for the 60-player CME Group Tour Championship. World number one Nelly Korda finished seventh and will aim to win a second title of the season at the finale next week. England's Lottie Woad, also in the field for the finale, secured a top-10 finish. Duncan said she was "completely shocked" and thanked those who believed in her.
Golf.copy:
American Lindy Duncan was left "completely shocked" after winning her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd time of asking. The 35-year-old started Sunday's final round of The Annika with a one-shot lead and two late birdies saw her claim victory.

Duncan, who joined the tour in 2014, had only enjoyed one top-10 finish this season. But her three-under-par 67 saw her finish on 16 under at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida, two shots clear of her nearest challenger, South Korea's Choi Hye-jin .

Golf.title: 'I'm back': Patrick Reed (and these 9 others) earn PGA Tour cards
Golf.summary: Ten players earned PGA Tour cards via the DP World Tour on Sunday, including Patrick Reed, ex-LIV pros and a former delivery driver. The post ‘I’m back’: Patrick Reed (and these 9 others) earn PGA Tour cards appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Patrick Reed has secured a PGA Tour card for 2027 via the DP World Tour's season-long points race, which offers 10 cards. He finished second among players without full PGA Tour status, behind Eugenio Chacarra, who took the top spot and will also be in early Signature Events and the Players Championship. Reed left LIV earlier this year. He won in Dubai and Qatar and finished T2 in Bahrain, plus a T12 at the Masters and T10 at the PGA Championship.

The future of the 10-card pathway is uncertain, with the DP World Tour-PGA Tour alliance up in the air. Competition is expected to increase in 2027 with an influx of former LIV players. Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship on Sunday and finished third in the Race to Dubai, but was ineligible for a card because of his LIV season. Reed said the decision to leave LIV came with only one year to qualify, and that returning would let him play closer to home.
Golf.copy:
On Sunday in Dubai, Patrick Reed made it official. “I’m back,” he said as he accepted a metal PGA Tour card and flashed a wide grin. “It feels good.” Reed left LIV earlier this year and, facing a one-year ban from the PGA Tour, turned his attention to the DP World Tour, where he hoped to earn one of 10 PGA Tour cards available via the season-long points race.

He took the drama out of that quest in just a few tournaments, winning in Dubai, finishing T2 in Bahrain and winning in Qatar in three consecutive early season events. Add in a T12 at the Masters and a T10 at the PGA Championship and he’d wrapped up his return pre-summertime.

Golf.title: Tyrrell Hatton targets Ryder Cup return for Team Europe and major breakthrough after DP World Tour Championship win
Golf.summary: Tyrrell Hatton targets Ryder Cup return for Team Europe and major breakthrough after DP World Tour Championship win Sky Sports
bullets: Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates by five shots, closing with a six-under 66 for his ninth DP World Tour title. He finished the season third in the Race to Dubai behind Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra, having entered the two season-ending play-offs outside the top 50 after mainly playing LIV Golf this year.

The win lifts Hatton to second in the European Ryder Cup rankings ahead of next year's centenary contest at Adare Manor, and he said he wants to be on Luke Donald's team. It is the fourth win in six DP World Tour events for a former LIV Golf player, following Adrian Meronk, Chacarra and Jon Rahm. The new season starts at the BMW Australian PGA Championship from 26 to 29 November in Sydney.
Golf.copy:
Tyrrell Hatton has set his sights on a Ryder Cup return and challenging for majors next season after storming to a five-shot victory at the DP World Tour Championship. Hatton pulled clear of the field on the final day at Jumeirah Golf Estates, firing a six-under 66 to go one better than last week's runner-up finish at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and claim a ninth DP World Tour title.

The win sees him end the DP World Tour season third in the Race to Dubai rankings, behind Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra, having entered the two season-ending play-offs outside of the top 50 after predominantly playing on LIV Golf this year.

Golf.summary: DP World Tour confirms major 2027 announcement as Bryson DeChambeau decision looms Golfmagic
bullets: The DP World Tour has confirmed it will announce all 2027 memberships on Tuesday 17 November, after the application deadline passed on Sunday night. The announcement is expected to clarify the futures of several former LIV Golf players. Bryson DeChambeau has reportedly been offered an exclusive route onto the circuit, following his 2024 US Open win at Pinehurst, and a top-10 Race to Dubai finish could offer a possible route back to the PGA Tour in 2028.

LIV Golf has abandoned its proposed relaunch and is moving towards an orderly wind-down. Joaquin Niemann has reportedly agreed to play 15 to 20 DP World Tour events in 2027 on sponsor invitations, and Lucas Herbert is said to have agreed to play 15. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and Sergio Garcia are already set to feature on the circuit, and DeChambeau could also target the 2027 Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.
Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour has confirmed to GolfMagic that an official announcement on all 2027 memberships will be made on Tuesday 17 November, with the futures of several high-profile former LIV Golf stars expected to become clearer.

A DP World Tour spokesperson confirmed the news to GolfMagic just hours before the membership application deadline passed on Sunday night. The announcement follows the conclusion of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, where Tyrrell Hatton secured a five-shot victory and Rory McIlroy was crowned Race to Dubai champion for a joint-record eighth time and fifth consecutive season.

Golf.title: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy snatches Race to Dubai title as Tyrrell Hatton claims big win in season finale
Golf.summary: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy snatches Race to Dubai title as Tyrrell Hatton claims big win in season finale Sky Sports
bullets: Tyrrell Hatton won the DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates by five shots, finishing on 15 under after a closing six-under 66 that included four birdies in a six-hole stretch on the back nine. It was his ninth DP World Tour title and his sixth Rolex Series win, a week after finishing runner-up at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

Rory McIlroy finished second after a bogey-free 67 and overtook Eugenio Chacarra in the standings to win the Race to Dubai for a fifth successive season. It was his eighth Order of Merit title, matching Colin Montgomerie's record. Chacarra, who shared third on eight under with Oliver Lindell, narrowly missed out. The new season starts at the BMW Australian PGA Championship from 26 to 29 November, and McIlroy's next event is the Australian Open from 3 to 6 December.
Golf.copy:
Tyrrell Hatton stormed to a five-shot win at the DP World Tour Championship, where Rory McIlroy snatched Race to Dubai victory from Eugenio Chacarra. Hatton took a one-shot lead into the final day at Jumeirah Golf Estates and never relinquished top spot, pulling clear of the field with four birdies in a six-hole stretch on the back nine.

The Englishman posted a six-under 66 to end on 15 under and claim a ninth DP World Tour title, as McIlroy leapfrogged Chacarra in the season-long standings with a runner-up finish after a thrilling Sunday tussle.

Golf.copy:
University of Miami golfer Scarlett Schremmer has been disqualified from The Annika due to using an illegal green-reading book during competition. Making her LPGA Tour debut after Kai Trump was forced to withdraw due to injury, Schremmer shot 69 and 74 to miss the cut anyway at Pelican Golf Club before the transgression was confirmed.

According to Golfweek's Beth Ann Nichols, who broke the story, the LPGA Tour initially learned of Schremmer's potential violation after her playing partners reported the issue following round one, but officials failed to take action until the weekend.

Golf.summary: Stars including Koepka and Aberg will play in the final event of the PGA Tour season, as well as players battling for full playing privileges
bullets: Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka and former champion Ludvig Aberg are in the field for the RSM Classic, the final PGA Tour event of the season, at Sea Island Golf Club in Georgia. Koepka makes his first PGA Tour start since finishing T67 at the Wyndham Championship in August, while Aberg seeks a second title after winning the event in 2023.

Following the tournament, only the top 100 in the rankings not otherwise exempt will earn full PGA Tour playing privileges for 2027, so many players have more at stake than usual. Matt Wallace, Christiaan Bezuidenhout, Max Greyserman, Billy Horschel and Lucas Glover are among those still uncertain of a place. Defending champion Sami Valimaki, Keegan Bradley, Brian Harman and Michael Brennan, who has two wins this year, are also playing.
Golf.copy:
Five-time Major winner Brooks Koepka and former champion Ludvig Aberg are among the big names in the field for the final PGA Tour event of the season, the RSM Classic. The tournament, which takes place at Sea Island Golf Club in Georgia, will also see several notable names battling to secure full PGA Tour status for 2027 as the FedExCup Fall concludes.

Koepka will be making his first PGA Tour start since placing T67 at the Wyndham Championship in August. Meanwhile, Aberg will be hoping to win the RSM Classic for the second time, having claimed his maiden PGA Tour title at the event in 2023.

Golf.title: The rise and fall of LIV Golf: How a $5 billion illusion met reality
Golf.summary: The rise and fall of LIV Golf: How a $5 billion illusion met reality The New York Times
bullets: LIV Golf admitted defeat on 5 November and has begun winding down its operations following a bankruptcy filing, after a scramble to find a new funding partner. CEO Scott O'Neil was told to shut the league down less than 16 months after a January 2025 meeting in Saudi Arabia, where chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan of the Public Investment Fund told him he had all the time he needed.

Under former CEO Greg Norman, billions were spent while a lack of revenue cost the league hundreds of millions in its first three years. The piece puts total spending at about $5bn. Jimmy Dunne, who negotiated the June 2023 framework agreement with the PGA Tour, said LIV had lost its funding backer, the near-trillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund.
Golf.copy:
In his first month on the job, LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil flew to Saudi Arabia to learn just how much time he had. O’Neil met with his new boss, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund and LIV’s chairman, to discuss the situation their league faced. Under former CEO Greg Norman, billions had been spent, but a shocking lack of revenue cost the league hundreds of millions in its first three years.

During the January 2025 meeting, O’Neil laid out two paths, according to multiple sources briefed on the meeting who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to do so publicly. One would be painful — dramatically trim the league’s exorbitant expenses, lay off employees, and do everything possible to get the balance sheet under control immediately. The other was a seven-year plan, built around maintaining LIV’s structure but gradually squeezing costs.

Legendary sports broadcaster Dan Hicks, one of the most well-known voices in golf, has died at the age of 64. The NBC Golf play-by-play announcer had been in his role since 2000 and commentated on a vast number of iconic moments within the sport such as Tiger Woods' famous 2008 US Open triumph and JJ Spun's 64-foot monster putt at Oakmont in 2025.

Hannah Storm, Hicks' wife and fellow announcer, confirmed his death in a statement on Thursday. Storm shared that Hicks had been suffering with an "acute illness" but his passing was "sudden" and unexpected. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Golf.summary: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy 'trending well' in pursuit of record-equalling Race to Dubai victory Sky Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy opened the season-ending DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates with a 69, leaving him two shots behind early leader Joost Luiten and three clear of Eugenio Chacarra, the player ahead of him in the Race to Dubai standings. The world No 2 is chasing an eighth Race to Dubai title and a fifth in a row, which would equal Colin Montgomerie's tally of eight Order of Merit wins.

Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley said McIlroy generally delivers when he has a clear goal, and described the title race as a three-horse contest between McIlroy, Chacarra and Rahm. Nine players began the week with a mathematical chance, but Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper, Aaron Rai and Ryan Fox all made poor starts. McIlroy, now 37, won his first Order of Merit in 2012 and said he has never lost his enthusiasm for the game.
Golf.copy:
Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley believes Race to Dubai victory will boost Rory McIlroy’s ambition to be remembered as the best European golfer of all-time. McIlroy arrived at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship second in the season-long standings, with the world No 2 looking to win the Race to Dubai for an eighth time and a fifth year in a row.

Winning the Harry Vardon Trophy would see him match Colin Montgomerie's tally of eight Order of Merit titles, with McIlroy making a strong start by posting an opening-round 69 at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

Golf.summary: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy boosts Race to Dubai hopes as Joost Luiten grabs shock early lead Sky Sports
bullets: Rory McIlroy opened with a three-under 69 at the DP World Tour Championship at Jumeirah Golf Estates, leaving him tied third and two shots behind Joost Luiten, who leads after a five-under 67. McIlroy made five birdies and two bogeys. He needs to finish fourth or better to have a chance of overtaking Eugenio Chacarra and winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title.

Chacarra, the Race to Dubai leader, opened with a level-par 72. McIlroy can guarantee the title by winning the event for a fourth time. Luiten, the last player in the field and 56th in the season rankings, is one ahead of Jacob Skov Olesen. Jon Rahm and Daniel Hillier also broke par with 71s, and only 22 of the 50 players finished under par. Olesen is among those seeking PGA Tour membership, which goes to the top 10 eligible players in the standings.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy made a strong start to his bid for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, as Joost Luiten grabbed a shock early lead at the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy, who needs to finish fourth or better to have a chance of surpassing Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings and win the Race to Dubai for an eighth time, carded an opening-round 69 at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

The world No 2 mixed five birdies with two bogeys in breezy conditions on the Earth Course, where he missed an eagle opportunity at the par-five last that would have moved him above Chacarra in the projected Race to Dubai standings.

Golf.copy:
Kota Kaneko has been named the Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year for 2026, becoming the second Japanese player to win the DP World Tour’s prestigious award. Kaneko lit up his debut season with a two-week stretch in May as he finished runner-up at the Soudal Open and won the Austrian Alpine Open presented by Kitzbühel Tirol seven days later.

He recorded a further four top 20 finishes to qualify as one of the leading 50 available players in the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World competing in the season-ending DP World Tour Championship.

Golf.title: Brutal New Slow-Play Rules Coming For 2027 With LPGA Tour ‘Heading In The Wrong Direction’
Golf.summary: Brutal New Slow-Play Rules Coming For 2027 With LPGA Tour ‘Heading In The Wrong Direction’ Golf Monthly
Golf.copy:
Despite plenty of penalties being handed out for slow play, the LPGA Tour was actually getting slower this year according to its data - so the tour has introduced even tougher sanctions to speed things up in 2027.

Timing data for the year showed penalties increased, the number of timed holes went up 12 percent and although overall the pace of play flatlined, the average time of twosomes in tournament play actually increased by seven minutes.
